partTitle: Part I - The Union and its Territory
partDesc: Articles 1 to 4, along with omitted Article 2A, covering the Union, territory, and formation of states.

articles.title: Article 1: Name and territory of the Union
articles.preview: India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States...
articles.text: Article 1. Name and territory of the Union.—`n(1) India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.`n1[(2) The States and the territories thereof shall be as specified in the First Schedule.]`n(3) The territory of India shall comprise—`n(a) the territories of the States;`n2[(b) the Union territories specified in the First Schedule; and]`n(c) such other territories as may be acquired.`nAmendment:`n1 Clause (2) was substituted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 2 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).`n2 Sub-clause (b) of Clause (3) was substituted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 2 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).
articles.simplified: Summary Note: India is defined by a dual name - India, that is Bharat. The Article describes India as a Union of States, meaning the Union is not a mere agreement among States and no State has a right to secede. It also explains that the territory of India includes the territories of States, the Union Territories listed in the First Schedule, and any territories that may be acquired in future.
articles.hindi:
1. संघ का नाम और राज्यक्षेत्र
(1) भारत, अर्थात इंडिया, राज्यों का संघ होगा।
(2) राज्यों और उनके राज्यक्षेत्र पहली अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट होंगे।
(3) भारत के राज्यक्षेत्र में शामिल होंगे:
(क) राज्यों के राज्यक्षेत्र;
(ख) पहली अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट संघ राज्यक्षेत्र; और
(ग) ऐसे अन्य राज्यक्षेत्र जो अर्जित किए जाएं।

articles.title: Article 2: Admission or establishment of new States
articles.preview: Parliament may by law admit into the Union, or establish, new States...
articles.text: Article 2. Admission or establishment of new States.— Parliament may by law admit into the Union, or establish, new States on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: This Article gives Parliament the power to admit new States into the Union or establish new States. It also allows Parliament to decide the terms and conditions on which such admission or establishment will take place.
articles.hindi:
2. नए राज्यों का प्रवेश या स्थापना
संसद विधि द्वारा ऐसे निबंधनों और शर्तों पर, जिन्हें वह उचित समझे, संघ में नए राज्यों का प्रवेश करा सकती है या नए राज्यों की स्थापना कर सकती है।

articles.title: Article 2A: Sikkim to be associated with the Union [Omitted]
articles.preview: Article 2A, relating to Sikkim being associated with the Union, was later omitted by amendment.
articles.text: Article 2A. [Sikkim to be associated with the Union.] — Omitted by the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975, s. 5 (w.e.f. 26-4-1975).`nAmendment:`nThis article was originally inserted by the Constitution (Thirty-fifth Amendment) Act, 1974, s. 2 (w.e.f. 1-3-1975), which was subsequently omitted by the 36th Amendment.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: Article 2A was a temporary provision dealing with Sikkim's association with the Union. It was first inserted through the 35th Amendment, but later removed by the 36th Amendment when Sikkim became a full-fledged State of India.
articles.hindi:
2क. [सिक्किम का संघ के साथ सहयुक्त किया जाना]
यह अनुच्छेद संविधान (छत्तीसवां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1975 द्वारा लोप किया गया।
संशोधन टिप्पणी: यह अनुच्छेद पहले संविधान (पैंतीसवां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1974 द्वारा जोड़ा गया था।

articles.title: Article 3: Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States
articles.preview: Parliament may by law form new States, increase or diminish the area of any State, alter boundaries, or change the name of any State, subject to the constitutional procedure.
articles.text: Article 3. Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States.—`nParliament may by law—`n(a) form a new State by separation of territory from any State or by uniting two or more States or parts of States or by uniting any territory to a part of any State;`n(b) increase the area of any State;`n(c) diminish the area of any State;`n(d) alter the boundaries of any State;`n(e) alter the name of any State:`n1[Provided that no Bill for the purpose shall be introduced in either House of Parliament except on the recommendation of the President and unless, where the proposal contained in the Bill affects the area, boundaries or name of any of the States2***, the Bill has been referred by the President to the Legislature of that State for expressing its views thereon within such period as may be specified in the reference or within such further period as the President may allow and the period so specified or allowed has expired.]`n3[Explanation I.—In this article, in clauses (a) to (e), “State” includes a Union territory, but in the proviso, “State” does not include a Union territory. Explanation II.—The power conferred on Parliament by clause (a) includes the power to form a new State or Union territory by uniting a part of any State or Union territory to any other State or Union territory.]`nAmendment:`n1 Subs. by the Constitution (Fifth Amendment) Act, 1955, s. 2, for the proviso (w.e.f. 24-12-1955).`n2 The words and letters "specified in Part A or Part B of the First Schedule" omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).`n3 Ins. by the Constitution (Eighteenth Amendment) Act, 1966, s. 2 (w.e.f. 27-8-1966).
articles.simplified: Summary Note: Article 3 deals with the internal reorganisation of India. Parliament can create new States, enlarge or reduce their areas, alter boundaries, or change names. The procedure requires a Presidential recommendation, and the affected State Legislature must be given an opportunity to express its views. However, Parliament is not bound by the State Legislature's opinion and may proceed even if the State disagrees.

articles.title: Article 4: Laws made under articles 2 and 3 to provide for the amendment of the First and the Fourth Schedules
articles.preview: A law made under Article 2 or Article 3 may amend the First and Fourth Schedules and include supplemental, incidental, and consequential provisions, and such a law is not treated as a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
articles.text: Article 4. Laws made under articles 2 and 3 to provide for the amendment of the First and the Fourth Schedules and supplemental, incidental and consequential matters.—`n(1) Any law referred to in article 2 or article 3 shall contain such provisions for the amendment of the First Schedule and the Fourth Schedule as may be necessary to give effect to the provisions of the law and may also contain such supplemental, incidental and consequential provisions (including provisions as to representation in Parliament and in the Legislature or Legislatures of the State or States affected by such law) as Parliament may deem necessary.`n(2) No such law as aforesaid shall be deemed to be an amendment of this Constitution for the purposes of article 368.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: Any law made under Article 2 or Article 3 may automatically make the changes needed in the First Schedule and the Fourth Schedule. Most importantly, such a law is not treated as a constitutional amendment under Article 368. This means Parliament can redraw territorial arrangements through a simple majority instead of the special amendment procedure.
articles.hindi:
4. अनुच्छेद 2 और 3 के अधीन बनाई गई विधियां
(1) अनुच्छेद 2 या अनुच्छेद 3 के अधीन बनाई गई विधि में पहली अनुसूची और चौथी अनुसूची में आवश्यक संशोधन किए जा सकते हैं, तथा अनुपूरक, आनुषंगिक और पारिणामिक उपबंध जोड़े जा सकते हैं。
(2) ऐसी कोई विधि अनुच्छेद 368 के प्रयोजनों के लिए संविधान का संशोधन नहीं मानी जाएगी।

partDesc: Articles 5 to 11 governing Indian citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

articles.title: Article 5: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
articles.preview: At the commencement of this Constitution, every person who has his domicile in the territory of India andâ€” (a) who was born in the territory of India; or (b) either of whose parents was born in the territory of India; or (c) who has been ordinarily resident in the territory of India for not less than five years...
articles.text: Article 5. Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.— At the commencement of this Constitution, every person who has his domicile in the territory of India and—`n(a) who was born in the territory of India; or`n(b) either of whose parents was born in the territory of India; or`n(c) who has been ordinarily resident in the territory of India for not less than five years immediately preceding such commencement, shall be a citizen of India.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: Covers people living in India on January 26, 1950. You became a citizen if you had a permanent home (domicile) in India and met any one of these: (a) You were born in India, (b) Either of your parents was born in India, or (c) You lived in India for at least 5 years just before the Constitution started.

articles.title: Article 6: Rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan
articles.preview: Notwithstanding anything in article 5, a person who has migrated to the territory of India from the territory now included in Pakistan shall be deemed to be a citizen of India at the commencement of this Constitution if he or either of his parents or any of his grand-parents was born in India as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935...
articles.text: Article 6. Rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan.— Notwithstanding anything in article 5, a person who has migrated to the territory of India from the territory now included in Pakistan shall be deemed to be a citizen of India at the commencement of this Constitution if—`n(a) he or either of his parents or any of his grand-parents was born in India as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935 (as originally enacted); and`n(b)(i) in the case where such person has so migrated before the nineteenth day of July, 1948, he has been ordinarily resident in the territory of India since the date of his migration, or`n(ii) in the case where such person has so migrated on or after the nineteenth day of July, 1948, he has been registered as a citizen of India by an officer appointed in that behalf by the Government of the Dominion of India on an application made by him therefor to such officer before the commencement of this Constitution in the form and manner prescribed by that Government:`nProvided that no person shall be so registered unless he has been resident in the territory of India for at least six months immediately preceding the date of his application.
articles.simplified:
Summary Note: Covers people who moved from Pakistan to India. They became citizens if they, their parents, or grandparents were born in undivided India and:
• Before July 19, 1948: They lived in India since their arrival.
• On/After July 19, 1948: They registered with the government after living in India for at least 6 months.

articles.title: Article 7: Rights of citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan
articles.preview: Notwithstanding anything in articles 5 and 6, a person who has after the first day of March, 1947, migrated from the territory of India to the territory now included in Pakistan shall not be deemed to be a citizen of India.
articles.text: Article 7. Rights of citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan.— Notwithstanding anything in articles 5 and 6, a person who has after the first day of March, 1947, migrated from the territory of India to the territory now included in Pakistan shall not be deemed to be a citizen of India:`nProvided that nothing in this article shall apply to a person who, after having so migrated to the territory now included in Pakistan, has returned to the territory of India under a permit for resettlement or permanent return issued by or under the authority of any law and every such person shall for the purposes of clause (b) of article 6 be deemed to have migrated to the territory of India after the nineteenth day of July, 1948.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: Covers people who left India for Pakistan after March 1, 1947. The Rule: They ceased to be Indian citizens. The Exception: If they returned to India with a legal resettlement permit, they could regain citizenship (following the same 6-month registration rule as in Article 6).

articles.title: Article 8: Rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India
articles.preview: Notwithstanding anything in article 5, any person who or either of whose parents or any of whose grand-parents was born in India as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935, and who is ordinarily residing in any country outside India as so defined shall be deemed to be a citizen of India...
articles.text: Article 8. Rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India.— Notwithstanding anything in article 5, any person who or either of whose parents or any of whose grand-parents was born in India as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935 (as originally enacted), and who is ordinarily residing in any country outside India as so defined shall be deemed to be a citizen of India if he has been registered as a citizen of India by the diplomatic or consular representative of India in the country where he is for the time being residing on an application made by him therefor to such diplomatic or consular representative, whether before or after the commencement of this Constitution, in the form and manner prescribed by the Government of the Dominion of India or the Government of India.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: Covers Indians living in other countries (like the UK or USA) at the time. They could become citizens if they, their parents, or grandparents were born in undivided India. Requirement: They must register themselves as Indian citizens through the Indian Embassy or Consulate in the country where they live.

articles.title: Article 9: Persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State not to be citizens
articles.preview: No person shall be a citizen of India by virtue of article 5, or be deemed to be a citizen of India by virtue of article 6 or article 8, if he has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of any foreign State.
articles.text: Article 9. Persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State not to be citizens.— No person shall be a citizen of India by virtue of article 5, or be deemed to be a citizen of India by virtue of article 6 or article 8, if he has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of any foreign State.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: A very strict rule: If you voluntarily acquire the citizenship of any foreign country, you automatically lose your Indian citizenship. India does not allow holding two passports (dual citizenship) simultaneously.

articles.title: Article 10: Continuance of the rights of citizenship
articles.preview: Every person who is or is deemed to be a citizen of India under any of the foregoing provisions of this Part shall, subject to the provisions of any law that may be made by Parliament, continue to be such citizen.
articles.text: Article 10. Continuance of the rights of citizenship.— Every person who is or is deemed to be a citizen of India under any of the foregoing provisions of this Part shall, subject to the provisions of any law that may be made by Parliament, continue to be such citizen.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: This ensures stability. Anyone who is a citizen under Articles 5 to 8 will continue to be a citizen, but this is always subject to any new laws passed by the Parliament.

articles.title: Article 11: Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law
articles.preview: Nothing in the foregoing provisions of this Part shall derogate from the power of Parliament to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.
articles.text: Article 11. Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.— Nothing in the foregoing provisions of this Part shall derogate from the power of Parliament to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.
articles.simplified: Summary Note: This clarifies that Articles 5–10 were mostly for citizenship at the time of independence. It gives the Parliament full power to make any future laws regarding the acquisition, termination, or any other matter related to citizenship (which led to the Citizenship Act of 1955).

partDesc: Articles 12 to 35 encompassing the basic rights of all persons and citizens.

articles.title: Article 12: Definition
articles.preview: In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires, 'the State' includes the Government and Parliament of India and the Government and the Legislature of each of the States and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.

articles.title: Article 13: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights
articles.preview: All laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution, in so far as they are inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.

articles.title: Article 14: Equality before law
articles.preview: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

articles.title: Article 15: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
articles.preview: The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them.

articles.title: Article 21: Protection of life and personal liberty
articles.preview: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

articles.title: Article 32: Remedies for enforcement of rights
articles.preview: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed.

partTitle: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
partDesc: Articles 36 to 51 encompassing the policy guidelines for the State.

articles.title: Article 36: Definition
articles.preview: In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires, “the State” has the same meaning as in Part III.
articles.text: Article 36. Definition.— In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires, “the State” has the same meaning as in Part III.

articles.title: Article 37: Application of the principles contained in this Part
articles.preview: The provisions contained in this Part shall not be enforceable by any court, but the principles therein laid down are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country...
articles.text: Article 37. Application of the principles contained in this Part.— The provisions contained in this Part shall not be enforceable by any court, but the principles therein laid down are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

articles.title: Article 38: State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people
articles.preview: The State shall strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting as effectively as it may a social order in which justice, social, economic and political, shall inform all the institutions of the national life.
articles.text: Article 38. State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people.—`n1[(1)] The State shall strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting as effectively as it may a social order in which justice, social, economic and political, shall inform all the institutions of the national life.`n2[(2) The State shall, in particular, strive to minimise the inequalities in income, and endeavour to eliminate inequalities in status, facilities and opportunities, not only amongst individuals but also amongst groups of people residing in different areas or engaged in different vocations.]`nAmendments:`n1 Art. 38 renumbered as cl. (1) by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 9 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979).`n2 Ins. by s. 9, ibid. (w.e.f. 20-6-1979).

articles.title: Article 39: Certain principles of policy to be followed by the State
articles.preview: The State shall direct its policy towards securing equal pay for equal work, adequate livelihood, and preventing the concentration of wealth.
articles.text: Article 39. Certain principles of policy to be followed by the State.— The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing—`n(a) that the citizens, men and women equally, have the right to an adequate means of livelihood;`n(b) that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good;`n(c) that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment;`n(d) that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women;`n(e) that the health and strength of workers, men and women, and the tender age of children are not abused and that citizens are not forced by economic necessity to enter avocations unsuited to their age or strength;`n1[(f) that children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner and in conditions of freedom and dignity and that childhood and youth are protected against exploitation and against moral and material abandonment.]`nAmendments:`n1 Subs. by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, s. 7, for cl. (f) (w.e.f. 3-1-1977).

articles.title: Article 39A: Equal justice and free legal aid
articles.preview: The State shall secure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice, on a basis of equal opportunity, and shall, in particular, provide free legal aid...
articles.text: 1[Article 39A. Equal justice and free legal aid.— The State shall secure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice, on a basis of equal opportunity, and shall, in particular, provide free legal aid, by suitable legislation or schemes or in any other way, to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.]`nAmendments:`n1 Ins. by s. 8, ibid. (w.e.f. 3-1-1977).

articles.title: Article 40: Organisation of village panchayats
articles.preview: The State shall take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
articles.text: Article 40. Organisation of village panchayats.— The State shall take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.

articles.title: Article 41: Right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases
articles.preview: The State shall, within the limits of its economic capacity and development, make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education and to public assistance...
articles.text: Article 41. Right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases.— The State shall, within the limits of its economic capacity and development, make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, and in other cases of undeserved want.

articles.title: Article 42: Provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief
articles.preview: The State shall make provision for securing just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief.
articles.text: Article 42. Provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.— The State shall make provision for securing just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief.

articles.title: Article 43: Living wage, etc., for workers
articles.preview: The State shall endeavour to secure, by suitable legislation or economic organisation or in any other way, to all workers, agricultural, industrial or otherwise, work, a living wage...
articles.text: Article 43. Living wage, etc., for workers.— The State shall endeavour to secure, by suitable legislation or economic organisation or in any other way, to all workers, agricultural, industrial or otherwise, work, a living wage, conditions of work ensuring a decent standard of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities and, in particular, the State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas.

articles.title: Article 43A: Participation of workers in management of industries
articles.preview: The State shall take steps, by suitable legislation or in any other way, to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings, establishments or other organisations engaged in any industry.
articles.text: 1[Article 43A. Participation of workers in management of industries.— The State shall take steps, by suitable legislation or in any other way, to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings, establishments or other organisations engaged in any industry.]`nAmendments:`n1 Ins. by s. 9, ibid. (w.e.f. 3-1-1977).

articles.title: Article 43B: Promotion of co-operative societies
articles.preview: The State shall endeavour to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control and professional management of co-operative societies.
articles.text: 1[Article 43B. Promotion of co-operative societies.— The State shall endeavour to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control and professional management of co-operative societies.]`nAmendments:`n1 Ins. by the Constitution (Ninety-seventh Amendment) Act, 2011, s. 3 (w.e.f. 15-2-2012).

articles.title: Article 44: Uniform civil code for the citizens
articles.preview: The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.
articles.text: Article 44. Uniform civil code for the citizens.— The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.

articles.title: Article 45: Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years
articles.preview: The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
articles.text: 1[Article 45. Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years.— The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.]`nAmendments:`n1 Subs. by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, s. 3, for art. 45 (w.e.f. 1-4-2010).

articles.title: Article 46: Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections
articles.preview: The State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes...
articles.text: Article 46. Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections.— The State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, and shall protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.

articles.title: Article 47: Duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health
articles.preview: The State shall regard the raising of the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties...
articles.text: Article 47. Duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health.— The State shall regard the raising of the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties and, in particular, the State shall endeavour to bring about prohibition of the consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health.

articles.title: Article 48: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry
articles.preview: The State shall endeavour to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and shall, in particular, take steps for preserving and improving the breeds...
articles.text: Article 48. Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry.— The State shall endeavour to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and shall, in particular, take steps for preserving and improving the breeds, and prohibiting the slaughter, of cows and calves and other milch and draught cattle.

articles.title: Article 48A: Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wild life
articles.preview: The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wild life of the country.
articles.text: 1[Article 48A. Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wild life.— The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wild life of the country.]`nAmendments:`n1 Ins. by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, s. 10 (w.e.f. 3-1-1977).

articles.title: Article 49: Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance
articles.preview: It shall be the obligation of the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest, declared by or under law made by Parliament to be of national importance...
articles.text: Article 49. Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance.— It shall be the obligation of the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest, 1[declared by or under law made by Parliament] to be of national importance, from spoliation, disfigurement, destruction, removal, disposal or export, as the case may be.`nAmendments:`n1 Subs. by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 27, for "declared by Parliament by law" (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).

articles.title: Article 50: Separation of judiciary from executive
articles.preview: The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.
articles.text: Article 50. Separation of judiciary from executive.— The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

articles.title: Article 51: Promotion of international peace and security
articles.preview: The State shall endeavour to promote international peace and security, maintain just and honourable relations between nations...
articles.text: Article 51. Promotion of international peace and security.— The State shall endeavour to—`n(a) promote international peace and security;`n(b) maintain just and honourable relations between nations;`n(c) foster respect for international law and treaty obligations in the dealings of organised peoples with one another; and`n(d) encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

partDesc: Article 51A highlighting the eleven duties of every Indian citizen.

articles.title: Article 51A: Fundamental Duties
articles.preview: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to abide by the Constitution, cherish its ideals, defend the country, and promote harmony.
articles.text: 1[PART IVA - FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES`n51A. Fundamental duties.— It shall be the duty of every citizen of India—`n(a) to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem;`n(b) to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom;`n(c) to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India;`n(d) to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so;`n(e) to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women;`n(f) to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture;`n(g) to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures;`n(h) to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform;`n(i) to safeguard public property and to abjure violence;`n(j) to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement; ]`n2[(k) who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.]`nAmendments:`n1 Ins. by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, s. 11 (w.e.f. 3-1-1977).`n2 Ins. by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, s. 4 (w.e.f. 1-4-2010).

partDesc: Articles 52 to 151 dealing with the President, Parliament, and Supreme Court.

articles.title: Article 52: The President of India
articles.preview: There shall be a President of India.
articles.text: There shall be a President of India.
articles.simplified: India will always have a President as the head of state.

articles.title: Article 74: Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
articles.preview: There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head...
articles.text: (1) There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.
articles.simplified: The President must act on the advice of the Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister.

articles.title: Article 124: Establishment and constitution of Supreme Court
articles.preview: There shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice of India...
articles.text: (1) There shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice of India and, until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number, of not more than seven other Judges.
articles.simplified: Establishes the Supreme Court of India, headed by the Chief Justice.

partDesc: Articles 152 to 237 dealing with State Executives, Legislature, and High Courts.

articles.title: Article 153: Governors of States
articles.preview: There shall be a Governor for each State...
articles.text: There shall be a Governor for each State: Provided that nothing in this article shall prevent the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more States.
articles.simplified: Every state must have a Governor. One person can also serve as the Governor for more than one state.

articles.title: Article 214: High Courts for States
articles.preview: There shall be a High Court for each State.
articles.text: There shall be a High Court for each State.
articles.simplified: Every state must have a High Court as its highest judicial body.

partDesc: Articles 239 to 242 covering administration of Union Territories.

articles.title: Article 239: Administration of Union territories
articles.preview: Every Union territory shall be administered by the President...
articles.text: (1) Save as otherwise provided by Parliament by law, every Union territory shall be administered by the President acting, to such extent as he thinks fit, through an administrator to be appointed by him...
articles.simplified: Union Territories are directly administered by the President through an appointed Administrator (like a Lieutenant Governor).

partDesc: Articles 243 to 243O dealing with rural local self-government.

articles.title: Article 243B: Constitution of Panchayats
articles.preview: There shall be constituted in every State, Panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels...
articles.text: (1) There shall be constituted in every State, Panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels in accordance with the provisions of this Part.
articles.simplified: Mandates a three-tier Panchayat system (village, intermediate, and district levels) in every state to ensure local self-government.

partDesc: Articles 243P to 243ZG dealing with urban local bodies.

articles.title: Article 243Q: Constitution of Municipalities
articles.preview: There shall be constituted in every State a Nagar Panchayat, a Municipal Council and a Municipal Corporation...
articles.text: (1) There shall be constituted in every Stateâ€” (a) a Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area; (b) a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area; and (c) a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area...
articles.simplified: Mandates three types of municipalities: Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations.

partTitle: Part X - The Scheduled and Tribal Areas
partDesc: Articles 244 to 244A.

articles.title: Article 244: Administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas
articles.preview: The provisions of the Fifth Schedule shall apply to the administration and control of the Scheduled Areas...
articles.text: (1) The provisions of the Fifth Schedule shall apply to the administration and control of the Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in any State other than the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
articles.simplified: Special administration rules apply to Scheduled and Tribal areas to protect indigenous populations.

partTitle: Part XI - Relations Between the Union and the States
partDesc: Articles 245 to 263 outlining legislative and administrative relations.

articles.title: Article 245: Extent of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States
articles.preview: Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India...
articles.text: (1) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India, and the Legislature of a State may make laws for the whole or any part of the State.
articles.simplified: Parliament makes laws for the whole country, while state legislatures make laws only for their respective states.

partTitle: Part XII - Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits
partDesc: Articles 264 to 300A (includes Right to Property).

articles.title: Article 300A: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law
articles.preview: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
articles.text: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
articles.simplified: The government cannot take away your property without a valid law allowing it. (This was formerly a Fundamental Right).

partTitle: Part XIII - Trade, Commerce and Intercourse
partDesc: Articles 301 to 307.

articles.title: Article 301: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse
articles.preview: Trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free.
articles.text: Subject to the other provisions of this Part, trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free.
articles.simplified: People are free to trade and do business anywhere across India without unreasonable barriers between states.

partTitle: Part XIV - Services Under the Union and the States
partDesc: Articles 308 to 323 including UPSC.

articles.title: Article 315: Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States
articles.preview: There shall be a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State...
articles.text: (1) Subject to the provisions of this article, there shall be a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State.
articles.simplified: Establishes the UPSC at the central level and State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs) at the state level to recruit civil servants.

partDesc: Articles 324 to 329A including Election Commission setup.

articles.title: Article 324: Election Commission
articles.preview: The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections...
articles.text: (1) The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to Parliament and to the Legislature of every State... shall be vested in a Commission.
articles.simplified: Creates an independent Election Commission of India to conduct free and fair elections across the country.

partTitle: Part XVI - Special Provisions Relating to Certain Classes
partDesc: Articles 330 to 342 dealing with SC/ST reservations.

articles.title: Article 330: Reservation of seats for SC and ST in the House of the People
articles.preview: Seats shall be reserved in the House of the People for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes...
articles.text: (1) Seats shall be reserved in the House of the People for â€” (a) the Scheduled Castes; (b) the Scheduled Tribes...
articles.simplified: Ensures that a certain number of seats in the Lok Sabha are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes based on their population.

partDesc: Articles 343 to 351.

articles.title: Article 343: Official language of the Union
articles.preview: The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.
articles.text: (1) The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.
articles.simplified: Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the central government, with English allowed for official work.

partDesc: Articles 352 to 360 covering National, State, and Financial Emergencies.

articles.title: Article 352: Proclamation of Emergency
articles.preview: If the President is satisfied that a grave emergency exists whereby the security of India is threatened...
articles.text: (1) If the President is satisfied that a grave emergency exists whereby the security of India or of any part of the territory thereof is threatened, whether by war or external aggression or armed rebellion, he may, by Proclamation, make a declaration to that effect...
articles.simplified: The President can declare a National Emergency if India's security is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

articles.title: Article 356: Failure of constitutional machinery in States
articles.preview: If the President is satisfied that the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution...
articles.text: (1) If the President, on receipt of a report from the Governor of a State or otherwise, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the Government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution, the President may by Proclamation assume to himself all or any of the functions of the Government of the State...
articles.simplified: Allows the central government to impose President's Rule in a state if the state government fails to function according to the Constitution.

partTitle: Part XX - Amendment of the Constitution
partDesc: Article 368 covering powers and procedure for amending the Constitution.

articles.title: Article 368: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution
articles.preview: Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision...
articles.text: (1) Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article.
articles.simplified: Gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution, but only by following a specific process (usually requiring a special majority).

partTitle: Part XXII - Short Title, Commencement, etc.
partDesc: Articles 393 to 395.

articles.title: Article 393: Short title
articles.preview: This Constitution may be called the Constitution of India.
articles.text: This Constitution may be called the Constitution of India.
articles.simplified: The official name of this document is the 'Constitution of India'.
